The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Bitcoin drops as Nvidia earnings report drives stock index futures higher. Bitcoin (BTC) is down 1.1% since midnight UTC at around $64,100, failing to keep pace with rising stock index futures after Nvidia beat earnings. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin outpaces gold even as both assets tumble ahead of a likely Fed rate hike. Bitcoin held near $64,000 as gold fell 2%, lifting the ratio between the two above its 200-day moving average and extending a series of higher lows since March. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Strategy stock could plunge 76% to $23, chart analyst warns. Aksel Kibar, who has tracked Bitcoin’s price action since at least 2018, made the bearish call, citing a still-active head-and-shoulders pattern on MicroStrategy’s (MSTR) daily chart. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Hyundai tests AI agent commerce on JPMorgan’s Kinexys blockchain. The exploration of AI agents with JPMorgan builds on Hyundai’s recent stablecoin-based cross-border remittance pilot. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Google finds self-running AI hacking tool with Russian comments in its files. Google spots an AI that can find and exploit software flaws on its own, no human needed. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live updates: Bitcoin stuck near $65,000 as popular 'basis trade' returns dry up. XRP edged toward $1 and SOL rose 3%, while a Talos report showed crypto’s favorite carry trade now pays about what Treasuries do. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $64,131 with a -1.12% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,797.57 with a -1.01% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto Today: ETF Outflows Accompany Mounting Selling Pressure on Bitcoin, Ethereum and XRP
items.description:
Slightly more than $1 billion left Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) last week through Friday, underscoring the waning appetite for crypto-related investment products over recent weeks. A third successive week of withdrawals takes cumulative outflows to $54.6 billion, with net assets under management at $86.2 billion. As these persistent withdrawals erode the institutional buffer against wider market price pressures, the likelihood of a prolonged sell-off increases. [...] Withdrawals from Ethereum spot ETFs reached $399 million last week through Friday, leaving the funds under continued bearish pressure. According to SoSoValue, this seventh consecutive week of outflows reduced cumulative inflows to $11.5 billion and net assets under management to $10.9 billion. [...] Roughly $19 million was withdrawn from XRP spot ETFs last week through Friday, a marked increase in weekly outflows. It was the second bearish week, following withdrawals of $530,000 in the week ending 6 November. Nevertheless, cumulative inflows remain at $1.8 billion, alongside net outflows of $1.2 billion, suggesting that investor interest in the underlying token remains positive and long-term.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Both Bitcoin and Ethereum funds have declined from their highs earlier in 2026. Bitcoin fund assets peaked at $128 billion in mid-January 2026, while Ethereum funds hit $21 billion the same day. Since then, both funds have dropped by about 15%.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.title: 2025 Crypto Regulatory Round-Up
items.description:
What is the GENIUS Act and how does it regulate stablecoins?

The GENIUS Act is United States legislation passed in 2025 that establishes a federal regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers. It mandates strict requirements for reserve backing, audits, and financial integrity. The law also places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign issued stablecoins, prompting a global acceleration in stablecoin policy development. [...] National regulators that have not yet developed or implemented stablecoin regulation will continue to make progress. By July 2026, U.S. federal and state regulators are required to promulgate final regulations to implement the GENIUS Act. This will include processes to license and regulate federal stablecoin issuers, and establishing criteria that foreign stablecoin issuers must meet in order to offer their stablecoins in the U.S. In Singapore, draft legislation to implement a stablecoin regime [...] We’re beginning to see regulation reconfigure usage patterns in the global stablecoin market, and that will increase over time. Europe has seen a rotation toward MiCA-compliant stablecoins as CASPs have been generally restricted from offering non-compliant ones. In the United States, the GENIUS Act places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign-issued stablecoins.
